Download prepared mortality rates from the Human Mortality Database

Source: R/construct_demographic_rates.R
get_mortality_hmd.Rd

Download a native HMD mortality product through HMDHFDplus. Male and female central death rates retain their person-year units and Hammel's piecewise constant hazard interpretation. Rates are not rescaled by age/period width. Missing retained rates are rejected. Optional open_age pools source deaths and exposure into a final open age band, permitting missing Mx in that tail.

Usage

get_mortality_hmd(
  country,
  year,
  username = Sys.getenv("HMD_USERNAME"),
  password = Sys.getenv("HMD_PASSWORD"),
  shape = "1x1",
  open_age = NULL
)

Arguments

country

A single HMD population code, such as "USA".

year

One whole-number calendar year or a nonempty vector of distinct years. For grouped HMD periods, supply their starting years. All requested years must exist in the product; duplicates are rejected.

username

Database username. Defaults to the HMD_USERNAME environment variable.

password

Database password. Defaults to the HMD_PASSWORD environment variable.

shape

Native HMD age-by-period shape: "1x1" (default), "1x5", "1x10", "5x1", "5x5", or "5x10". This selects Mx_<shape>; open_age can separately pool the final age band.

open_age

Optional nonnegative whole age at a native age-band start. Default NULL keeps the source age layout. Otherwise retain rates below this age and pool Deaths_<shape> and Exposures_<shape> into one [open_age, Inf) rate for each sex and source period: total deaths divided by total person-years. This requires two additional product downloads. Counts/exposures must be finite and nonnegative with positive pooled exposure; individual zero-exposure cells may contribute zero. No missing counts/exposures are imputed. Cutoffs must align with source bands (0, 1, 5, 10, etc. for five-year ages). The cutoff is not a maximum lifespan.

Value

A validated mortality rate tibble with a source attribute recording years, shape and represented source periods. Multiple-year requests include time_start/time_end; length-one requests omit them. With open_age, source metadata also records the pooling method, products and tail totals.

Details

A single requested year returns a static schedule without calendar columns. Multiple years return time_start/time_end for the selected source periods, in chronological order. For grouped-time shapes, year selects period starts: for example, 2000 selects the source interval 2000-2004 in a five-year product. Nonconsecutive requests retain calendar gaps; no rates are carried forward.

Native five-year ages are 0, 1-4, 5-9, etc.; returned bands are [0,1), [1,5), [5,10), etc. Upper-open ages end at Inf. Source period ends are inclusive and map to exclusive next-year endpoints. Shortened source periods are retained. Each required product is downloaded once per call. For grouped-time products, readers that discard period end labels also require one Mx_1x1 request to establish annual coverage; this is recorded in source metadata. Credentials are passed to the reader and never stored in the returned table.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rates <- get_mortality_hmd("USA", year = 2000)
saveRDS(rates, "rates.rds")
model <- hammel_model() |> set_mortality(readRDS("rates.rds"))
history <- get_mortality_hmd("SWE", year = 1891:2000, open_age = 95)
grouped <- get_mortality_hmd("SWE", year = seq(1900, 1995, 5),
  shape = "5x5", open_age = 95)
} # }
